name: Bill van Rij

work_experience.notes: Settled in Christchurch, New Zealand after emigrating from the Netherlands in 1951; worked for an ice cream company as a businessman
Participated in the founding of the Coalition of Concerned Citizens in 1985, a union of conservative (mainly Christian) lobby groups using the motto 'For God, Family and Country'

work_experience.organization: 新西兰基督教遗产党(Christian Heritage Party of New Zealand)
work_experience.notes: Principal founder of the Christian Heritage Party. Began the process of establishing the party in 1988; officially launched on 20 July 1989 with van Rij as president. Remained concerned mainly with organisational matters while John Allen served as interim political leader.

work_experience.organization: 新西兰基督教遗产党(Christian Heritage Party of New Zealand)
work_experience.position: 基督教联盟首席谈判代表
work_experience.notes: Strongly urged cooperation between Christian Heritage and the Christian Democrats; lobbied extensively for the establishment of the Christian Coalition in 1996. After the Coalition collapsed in May 1997, left Christian Heritage and joined the Christian Democrats.
Left Christian Heritage and joined the Christian Democrats after the Christian Coalition collapsed, blaming Graham Capill for the Coalition's failure

person_relationships.name: John Allen
person_relationships.notes: Allen served as interim political leader of the Christian Heritage Party while van Rij focused on organisational matters as president

person_relationships.name: Graham Capill
person_relationships.notes: Van Rij and Capill clashed over strategy, especially regarding cooperation with the Christian Democrats. Van Rij blamed Capill for the collapse of the Christian Coalition in 1997.

person_relationships.name: Graeme Lee
person_relationships.notes: Lee was the National MP who founded the Christian Democrats. Van Rij strongly supported cooperation with Lee's party and lobbied for the Christian Coalition.

person_relationships.name: Ed Vanwoudenberg
person_relationships.notes: Founder of the Christian Heritage Party of Canada; both were Dutch immigrants with connections to Reformed churches. Van Rij took direct inspiration from Vanwoudenberg's Canadian party.

person_relationships.name: Geoff Hounsell
person_relationships.notes: Former Deputy Leader of Christian Heritage who resigned alongside van Rij after the Christian Coalition collapsed

political_stances.stance: Van Rij believed that pressure groups were inadequate for promoting Christian values in politics and that only direct participation through a Christian political party would be effective

Initially supported confessionalism (requiring Christian belief for party membership) at the party's founding, but later prioritized unity between Christian parties, believing that cooperation was more important than ideological purity

political_stances.topic: 反堕胎、反色情、支持传统家庭
political_stances.stance: Strongly opposed abortion, pornography, and the perceived erosion of marriage and the family, consistent with the Christian Heritage Party's founding principles

biography_summary: 比尔·范赖（Bill van Rij）是新西兰基督教政治的重要人物，也是新西兰基督教遗产党（Christian Heritage Party）的主要创始人和首任主席。范赖出生于荷兰，1951年移居新西兰，在基督城定居后成为一名商人，从事冰淇淋公司的相关工作。他是虔诚的基督教徒，最初属于改革宗教会，后于1960年代初转投福音派长老会。1985年，范赖参与了'关切公民联盟'（Coalition of Concerned Citizens）的创建，该组织是保守派基督教游说团体的联合组织，以'为了上帝、家庭和国家'为口号。1987年工党连任后，范赖认为压力团体无法有效推动基督教价值观在政治领域的实现，开始相信只有通过建立基督教政党直接参与政治才能取得成效。他从加拿大基督教遗产党获得灵感——该党创始人埃德·范沃登伯格（Ed Vanwoudenberg）同样是一位荷兰裔移民，与改革宗教会有联系。范赖与范沃登伯格就基督教政治进行了深入讨论，并于1987年受邀参加了加拿大党的首次全国大会。1988年，范赖与几位朋友在马尔伯勒海峡的罗德·伊特威尔家中召开了预备会议，开始组建新西兰基督教遗产党。前国家党候选人约翰·艾伦担任临时政治领袖，范赖则主要负责组织事务。1989年7月20日，基督教遗产党正式成立，范赖出任首任主席。此后，格雷厄姆·卡皮尔被任命为党魁，但据信并非范赖所支持。范赖在党内最大贡献之一是推动基督教遗产党与格雷姆·李（Graeme Lee）创立的基督教民主党之间的合作。他担心基督教选票的分裂，强烈敦促两党进行谈判。尽管卡皮尔和'信仰告白派'抵制合并，范赖（虽然在建党时支持信仰告白制）认为团结至关重要。在他大力游说下，基督教联盟最终于1996年3月29日成立。然而，联盟在1996年大选中仅获4.33%选票，未能跨越5%门槛进入议会。选后两党互相指责，联盟于1997年5月解散。范赖对此深感失望，与副领袖杰夫·豪恩塞尔（Geoff Hounsell）等温和派一起威胁退出基督教遗产党，除非推进统一。最终范赖被要求辞职，随后转投基督教民主党，并公开指责卡皮尔导致联盟崩溃。范赖的政治遗产是深远的：他创建的基督教遗产党在其存续的17年间始终是新西兰最重要的基督教政党，1993年和1999年均成为议会外最大政党，并推动了新西兰MMP选举制度的采用。
